# Task Summary

Plan `PK-012 Product Visual System` as a shared foundation layer for the current Next.js App Router codebase. The work should turn the partially established `PK-001` home-page styling into reusable product-level foundations for typography, spacing, color, card/panel patterns, and responsive layout behavior without expanding into browse/detail feature implementation.

# Affected Area Summary

- `src/app/globals.css`
  - Primary source of truth for app-wide semantic design tokens, layout rhythm, motion policy, and baseline typography helpers.
- `src/app/layout.tsx`
  - Preserve the `next/font` setup and, if needed, make minor shell-level updates so the visual system is consistently applied at the app root.
- `src/components/ui/*` or `src/components/system/*`
  - Likely creation point for a small shared visual foundation layer if the implementation goes beyond tokens.
- `src/components/home/*`
  - First consumer of the shared foundations. Existing inline styling should be reduced where repeated patterns can move into shared primitives or shared class patterns.
- Future user-facing routes not yet present
  - `PK-002` and `PK-004` should be treated as downstream adopters, not implementation targets in this chunk.

# Implementation Approach

Center `PK-012` on shared foundations, not route-specific polish. The implementation should:

- establish a semantic token model for color, surfaces, text roles, spacing, radius, borders, and motion in `src/app/globals.css`
- keep `next/font` as the single typography entry point and define a documented type direction on top of it
- standardize responsive container and section spacing behavior that future routes can consume
- define a small set of reusable visual patterns for cards, panels, headings, and CTA treatments if repeated usage justifies extraction
- refactor the current home route to consume the new shared foundations so the system is exercised immediately

Implementation guidance:

- Keep all visual foundations server-component compatible. No client boundary is required for this chunk.
- Avoid speculative design-system breadth. Extract only patterns that are already repeated or clearly needed by upcoming browse/detail routes.
- Favor semantic, app-wide token naming over home-page-specific naming.
- Preserve a thin route-file architecture; route files should remain composition shells rather than token or style-definition owners.
- If shared components are created, keep them presentational and variant-explicit. Avoid boolean-prop-heavy abstractions.

# Architecture Notes

- Server/client boundary:
  - Default boundary remains server-side.
  - No `'use client'` is expected for tokens, layout primitives, or presentational wrappers.
- Data placement:
  - No new data fetching, route handlers, or mutations belong in this chunk.
  - The visual system should consume existing static content and remain independent of data-model concerns.
- Foundation ownership:
  - `src/app/globals.css` should own semantic tokens, spacing scale, motion defaults, and base global rules.
  - Shared components, if created, should own repeated structure and reusable variant boundaries, not theme definitions.
- Composition:
  - Prefer a small shared layer such as section container, heading block, card/panel wrappers, and CTA/link styles rather than a broad component library.
  - Existing home components should become consumers of the shared layer rather than continuing as the style source of truth.
- UX/accessibility:
  - Visual system decisions must preserve contrast, focus visibility, readable type scaling, and reduced-motion safety.
  - Responsive behavior should distinguish between spacious marketing layouts and denser future browse/detail surfaces.

# File Creation / Modification / Deletion Summary

- Modify `src/app/globals.css`
  - Replace route-biased token naming with reusable semantic tokens and codify spacing/layout foundations.
- Modify `src/app/layout.tsx`
  - Likely minor shell-level alignment only; keep font ownership here.
- Create `src/components/ui/*` or `src/components/system/*`
  - Optional but recommended if the chosen strategy includes a small shared visual layer.
- Modify `src/components/home/*`
  - Refactor current home components to consume shared foundations and validate the system against a real route.
- No route additions expected.
- No deletions expected.

# Execution Order

1. Choose the PK-012 depth: tokens only, or tokens plus a small shared UI/system layer.
2. Define the semantic token model and spacing/layout rules in `src/app/globals.css`.
3. Confirm any required shell-level adjustments in `src/app/layout.tsx` without changing route architecture.
4. Create the minimum shared visual primitives/pattern wrappers if that option is chosen.
5. Refactor `src/components/home/*` to consume the new shared tokens/patterns as the first in-repo adopter.
6. Verify the home route still renders coherently on desktop and mobile.
7. Run deterministic checks with `pnpm lint` and `pnpm build`.

# Verification Expectations

- Required automated checks:
  - `pnpm lint`
  - `pnpm build`
- Required manual verification:
  - confirm typography hierarchy remains readable across breakpoints
  - confirm shared card/panel treatments are visually coherent and accessible on `/`
  - confirm focus states, contrast, and reduced-motion behavior still hold after the refactor
  - confirm responsive container spacing does not regress the home route
- Test impact:
  - No test harness exists today, so do not introduce Vitest solely for visual-foundation work.
  - Once multiple routes exist, the right automated test layer is Playwright because the meaningful risk is responsive behavior, visual consistency, and navigation/accessibility semantics in the browser.

# Open Decisions

- Shared-foundation depth:
  - Option A: token-first only in `src/app/globals.css`
  - Option B: tokens plus a small shared UI/system layer for repeated cards, headings, containers, and CTA treatments
  - Recommendation: Option B. Tokens alone will improve naming, but they will leave repeated structural styling duplicated across current and future route components.
- Home-route adoption timing:
  - Option A: establish foundations now and leave the home route mostly as-is
  - Option B: refactor `src/components/home/*` immediately as the first consumer
  - Recommendation: Option B. Without a first consumer, the visual system remains unproven and is more likely to drift before browse/detail routes land.
- Token naming strategy:
  - Option A: keep current brand-centric names such as `--brand-red` and `--surface-strong`
  - Option B: migrate toward semantic role-based names for app-wide reuse
  - Recommendation: Option B. Future browse/detail density and surface needs will be easier to support with role-based naming than page-specific naming.
